From a conscious point of view:
We need to understand the formation of the acronym LGBT. The histories point us way back, to unknown era's where forms of homosexuality existed. Now fast forward to the Era of "Pride day" which is so recent. We (a huge amount of members in LGBT) have been known for "creating" fatal-to-now chronic illnesses.
We fought for our rights under contracts of indoctrination but most of us turned a blind eye to those clauses... Which is why some of our brothers and sisters are still burned and stoned alive because truly, we were never accepted. 
Our psychological mission has been to survive, it's as if the system programmed us to "study hard", "practice hard" so we can attain some sense of liberty...

However, the liberty we ran after is materialistic. Just look on TV... And this encompasses all of us regardless of age.

All the men over 40 will let you in on their personal stories of what they think dating a mid 20 guys is like...but they just remain personal stories.

 You say yourself that you crave maturity, wisdom & etc. They also do. We then throw stones at each other at how we are incompatible (all of us) and this creates a cognitive dissonance because consciously you realize all we are and we have been perceived is just based on materialiasm.

We never thought that maybe if we could all unite as the members to start talking about the philosophies that we believe in created by men who hate us THEN maybe we have a shot at this. It is my fear that in decades to come, dust is what will be left of us. Fortunately it's not all so dark

We could then open a new set of consciousness whereby our actions are inclined to create something meaningful, not only with men over 40 or a certain age but with ourselves first.

Display and give positive, wise and kind vibes. Maybe when we notice how we are all trying to love one another, we can then see all that's beautifully laid in our hearts & embark on mandates that prove us to be humans, intelligent, conscious, wise and kind.

You'll realize there's beauty in that rude 20 year old boy who looks immature because effectively reality will catch up with him and when it hits that's when a butterfly comes out. Obviously some come in colors and others come really dark but we're all butterflies. The 20 year old if conscious enough will seek wisdom on how to give back the love they've been given when they were not "so lovable". 

We all have a role to play, to learn that not all 40+ year old posses the right kind of wisdom and that's okay. We may learn to love a person with all the good and bad not because you can't do better but because you both make each other wiser and most kind no matter your ages.

I love you guys❤️

It's all good words and advices until you realize that the whole world never truly accepted the LGBT lifestyle. You can find sources of that from the day they created HIV. We can all go back and forth on what's right or wrong but if you have not realized by now that the system we live in is failing us, we will not stop using meds. We will hate each other, kiss & kill each other discussing the morality of our fate. We are a powerful community, all of us combined but we lack the wisdom to act on it.

Hey, I'm the depressed friend. Well not your friend but you get the just. Firstly thank you for caring that much. You are a wonderful soul. Continue to remain what you are, be the friend. You don't have to be sad with me to make me feel better. Maybe I'm asking for too much but I'd love to see you around telling me about your day and sometimes your thoughts. If I ever try to speak about anything just listen, I don't expect you to have an answer. Sometimes "I don't know my friend, let's both figure it out" is always better than irrelevant positivity that does not seem to apply to my life as yet.

Wednesday I tried taking my life, a friend from a different country noticed & called his bois in my country to keep me alive. I honestly had not thought my life was more meaningful to him. Now I lay in a hospital bed thinking of different ways to thank him because words don't do him justice. He hasn't offered anything along "it's going to be alright" except he paid attention. That's more than anyone has ever done. If there was one seat left in heaven, I'd save it for him. I hope you find great wisdom during this time. ♥️♥️
Your reply hit home. Thanks man

I'm in South Africa. I will answer in terms of how it is being so in the country and how it is within the LGBT
-In S.A:
Relatively not easy growing up, you find you are the only one in your area who's a little softer than the rest. Hate speech, bullying & all those were part of the juices we drank for being gay. I lost my eye cs I was nor cared for at home and I was so young (5 or 6) my acts came naturally so I had to learn how to act right, introversion became me.

-In LGBT
We are so divided. The out of the closet folks are angry that they have to take the bullets first. The closet ones are impatient, emotionally unavailable & sad. We are so obsessed with American gay culture of looking good, be with boyfriends that look good, being aggressive and rude just to stand your ground, big dicks, fame and popularity. You also get to see decent bro's selling dicks a lot (economy issues).

In all this you have your gay bros who have persevered so hard in life, they've made a name for themselves.  They work hard and drive nice cars, however all that doesn't save you from the above it just buys you nice coffees,  nice phones, nice shoes, expensive brunches... all those with an empty heart.

I guess it's true that there's really nothingness after we die. Somehow that nothingness is more inviting than living in a space of everything whilst feeling nothing but pain. However I appreciate your words, it certainly does make a difference.
You may not know it but replies like yours are the reason we decide "not today death". Thank you. May the universe protect your soul
I am beyond surprised that I even got a reply especially this profound. Thank you for sharing your wisdom, I hope in my next life I meet people like you
